newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coconut Oil - Prices seen softer on USDA report.
newsitem.headline: Coconut Oil - Prices seen softer on USDA report.

text.p: Coconut oil prices are expected to drift sideways or lower Philippine traders said on Monday, following the fall in Malaysian palm oil prices which slid on Friday's bearish USDA soybean crop report.
"I expect the market to open tentative to softer for the week due to the USDA soybean report and improving copra production on the local front," one trader told Reuters.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture said on Friday that 1996 soybean production would total 2.346 billion bushels, higher than the average trade estimate of 2.287 billion and above the USDA's September forecast of 2.270 billion.
The supply of copra on southern Mindanao island has also improved, putting further pressure on prices, an official of the government's Philippine Coconut Authority (PCA) said.
But traders said they do not expect any dramatic rise in supply in the next few days.
"I expect coconut oil exports to reach 75,000 tonnes this month," said one trader.

Philippine monthly coconut oil exports fell to an average 66,823 tonnes from January to September this year compared with an average of 113,940 tonnes a month last year, the private trade group United Coconut Associations of the Philippines (UCAP) said in a weekly report.
"I expect coconut oil prices to drop to $725 from $740 a tonne CIF for nearby months in Europe, and below the current price of 33.75 cents per lb CIF in the United States," said one trader.
UCAP said the Philippines exported 48,000 tonnes of coconut oil from October 1 to 10 and 12,000 tonnes of copra meal.
Reports of a copra supply crunch in Mindanao following a delayed harvest due to torrential rains ad sent prices soaring in the past few weeks.
"(The) copra harvest in Mindanao is our salvation. Luzon (harvest) is a goner," said one dealer.

Recovery is barely under way in coconut growing areas on Luzon island devastated by a string of typhoons last year which demolished up to 300,000 trees. The area accounts for 30 percent of the national crop.
Philippine coconut millers are now directly selling their products to buyers with the slight improvement in copra supply from Mindanao and some parts of Luzon island, traders said.
